name: Miami Beach / Sunset Harbour
notes: Sunset Harbour Yacht Club. Home base. Lincoln Rd walkable.

name: Boca Raton / Hillsboro Inlet
notes: When EXITING, keep close to the starboard/right side of the channel — bridge operator's advice (May 18, 2026) with waves breaking in the channel. Fair-weather inlet; respect a building swell.

name: Lake Worth / Palm Beach
notes: Lake Worth Inlet — deep, all-weather. Gulf Stream close to shore Palm Beach→Canaveral; stacks up in NE wind.

name: Fort Pierce
notes: Often called best all-weather inlet on the East Coast. Downtown marina walkable. Natural mid-leg bailout ~110nm from Palm Beach.

name: Cape Canaveral / Port Canaveral
notes: Deep commercial inlet, easy all-weather, good fuel. Watch cruise-ship traffic + security zone.

name: St. Augustine
notes: Bar SHOALS and shifts — cross at/near high tide ONLY. Favor current ATONs over chart. City Marina downtown by Bridge of Lions.

name: Fernandina Beach
notes: Deep, well-marked inlet. Fuel + protected overnight. Used as fog-diversion before St. Aug. Good contingency.

name: Brunswick / St. Simons
notes: Brunswick Landing 'Velcro Marina.' ~130nm from St. Aug. WWII hurricane hole. Solid mid-leg bailout.

name: Hilton Head / Harbour Town
notes: Sea Pines. Harbourmaster Leslie (843) 363-8335. Rick: great food at the Country Club, walking distance. Weather bailout/fuel.

name: Charleston
notes: Deep, well-marked all-weather harbor. Natural multi-day weather hold, full services. 5+ ft tidal range — real current on arrival. WARNING (Rick): do NOT run the ICW between here and Southport — it's poorly documented, markers off by 30-40 yards from actual deep water (confirmed by infrared/heat survey). Run outside on this stretch.

name: Winyah Bay / Georgetown
notes: Sea buoy well offshore; jetties demand respect on building southerly. Workable but not a casual entry.

name: Southport / Cape Fear River
notes: Cape Fear River entrance deep/commercial. Safe Harbor South Harbour Village — ask for Bill Gregory (910) 352-8469. Joseph's Italian Bistro at marina; Rick's pick Home Run Place north of bridge. WARNING (Rick): do NOT run the ICW between here and Charleston — poorly documented, markers off by 30-40 yards from actual deep water (confirmed by infrared/heat survey). Run outside on this stretch.

name: Wrightsville / Masonboro Inlet
notes: Masonboro Inlet — enter mid-to-high tide. Check Aqua Map shoaling MM 293.7. Hybrid ICW route option here.

name: Beaufort / Morehead City
notes: Beaufort Inlet deep all-weather commercial. KEY staging point for the Hatteras rounding. Full services, easy to sit out weather. Morehead City Yacht Basin dockmaster (252) 726-6862.

name: Cape Hatteras (offshore rounding)
notes: NOT a stop — the critical offshore rounding. Gulf Stream close offshore; wind-against-current sea builds fast over Diamond Shoals. Do NOT leave Beaufort without a confirmed window.

name: Coinjock (ICW)
notes: ICW MM 50, inside route. Dock EAST side (restaurant access). 32oz prime rib — call ahead (252) 453-3271. Tip dock hands in CASH not card (adds 20%).

name: Oregon Inlet
notes: Shoal and treacherous — treat as a position, not a reliable bailout.

name: Norfolk / Waterside (Hampton Roads)
notes: Waterside Marina downtown (757) 625-3625, new floating docks, MM 0. Heavy Navy/commercial traffic — they have right of way, monitor VHF 16. Bluewater Hampton backup (757) 723-6774.

name: Great Bridge Lock (ICW)
notes: NB opens on the hour, SB at :30. Miss it by 3 min = wait an hour. Gilmerton/NS#7 RR bridge pair nearby — 6kts, watch lights (green=clear, red=hold). 'The pair that nearly came down on you.'

name: Ocean City MD
notes: Notoriously shoal/dangerous in any onshore swell. Fair-weather ONLY.

name: Cape May NJ
notes: Deep reliable inlet, the safety valve for the NJ coast. South Jersey Marina (609) 884-2400 — books up fast. Lobster House next door. Enter from ocean side.

name: Atlantic City NJ
notes: ~30nm past Cape May. Golden Nugget (big basin) or Kammerman's (quieter, family-run). Absecon Inlet. Safety: stay near marina/boardwalk after dark.

name: Barnegat Light NJ
notes: MOST CRITICAL INLET. Previous incident here. Enter mid-FLOOD only, MORNING only, favor north jetty. Never on ebb, never afternoon, no NE swell. Bayview Harbor.

name: Manasquan NJ
notes: Better than Barnegat but tight. One of the few workable NJ inlets.

name: New York Harbor / Sandy Hook
notes: Ambrose Channel — heavy ship traffic, right of way, monitor VHF 16. Time Sandy Hook for fair current.

name: Liberty Landing (NYC)
notes: Jersey City, Liberty State Park. Calm basin, ferry to Manhattan. Dockmaster Janer (201) 985-8000. NYC overnight or weather bailout.

name: Port Washington NY (LI Sound)
notes: Manhasset Bay, protected. Municipal & Safe Harbor Capri. LIRR to Manhattan 35 min. Hell Gate runs hard — time the East River for fair current.

name: The Race / Plum Gut (LI Sound)
notes: NOT a stop — current gate at the east end of LI Sound. Runs hard; time for fair current.

name: Montauk NY
notes: Lake Montauk — straightforward entry, good fuel dock. ~130nm staging option between NJ and New England.

name: Block Island RI
notes: Great Salt Pond. Classic New England stop.

name: Newport RI
notes: Narragansett Bay — easy, well-marked entry. Home water for the New England end.

name: Cape Cod Canal
notes: Connects Buzzards Bay & Cape Cod Bay. Currents top 4-5kts. Monitor VHF 13 entire transit, hail Control 16 / working 12/14. 10mph limit, no wake — they cite violators. Time for slack/fair current.

name: Buzzards Bay / Falmouth MA
notes: East Falmouth / Green Pond. New England base. Falmouth Marine & MacDougalls on Dockwa.

name: Nantucket MA
notes: Nantucket Boat Basin (508) 325-1350, 2-night min, concierge. Nantucket Sound builds with afternoon SW against ebb — arrive before midday.

name: Chelsea Piers, Hudson River, New York City
